evidence: One typed ResolvedLaunch now owns bounded Codex whole-plugin and standalone-stdio-MCP selection, deterministic activation composition, admitted environment-variable names, isolation/provider identity and action-time source revalidation.
The bounded cardinality remains zero/one plugin plus zero/one standalone MCP; unsupported resource kinds, --with=all, multi-plugin, multi-MCP and overlapping plugin/MCP identities fail closed.

Focused regressions cover clean, plugin-only, MCP-only and composed plugin+MCP planning, deterministic argv ordering, overlap refusal, raw provider activation conflict, qualification/env negatives, source drift and sanitized inspection.

Exact-candidate macOS real-provider composition rehearsal requires selected plugin and MCP runtime evidence, sibling absence, environment admission, negative failure modes and task-owned process lifecycle closure.
The candidate changes only the clean-room-launcher package version from 0.4.7 to 0.5.0; runtime/build dependency versions and the locked dependency graph are unchanged.
Existing dependency review, cargo-deny, locked build/test and supply-chain metadata gates remain mandatory.
Release-candidate topology now runs the composition rehearsal on exact PR-candidate bytes and carries its evidence into the mandatory release graph.
The new rehearsal is wired through the existing release-eligibility/readiness topology rather than a parallel manual path.
Release Contract v1 now treats exact Codex plugin+MCP composition as a blocker-producing capability that must be rehearsed on the PR candidate and preserved in pre-tag stage evidence.
Accepted-main staging and pretag verification bind composition evidence to the exact future shipping archive before protected tag creation.

README, Codex/provider/configuration/limitations/Claude docs and CHANGELOG describe the bounded v0.5.0 composition and effective-launch inspection without widening unsupported transports, cardinality, platforms or Claude standalone MCP.

Human and JSON inspection claims are limited to sanitized identities, decisions, qualification state, environment-variable names and boundary metadata; provider argv values, secrets and private source paths are explicitly non-claims.

near_misses.failure_mode: A plugin or standalone MCP source can change after planning, leaving a composed launch partly bound to stale authority.
near_misses.durable_control: ResolvedLaunch retains both typed source plans and revalidates both before provider birth; focused mutation regressions require any one-side drift to invalidate the whole composed launch, and exact-provider rehearsal exercises the action-time boundary.

near_misses.failure_mode: A selected whole plugin can expose the same MCP identity as the separately selected standalone MCP, creating two activation authorities for one logical server.
near_misses.durable_control: Resolution compares the selected plugin MCP component IDs with the standalone MCP ID and fails closed on overlap before launch; raw provider config/plugin/MCP activation controls are also refused while CLROOM selection is active.

near_misses.failure_mode: A shared launch-plan inspection surface could serialize provider arguments, literal environment values, source paths or other private configuration while trying to explain the effective launch.
near_misses.durable_control: ResolvedLaunch emits a dedicated sanitized summary containing bounded identities/reasons, environment-variable names, boundary controls and provider-argv element count only; unit/CLI regressions reject provider argv values, secret values, cwd/source paths and other private material in human/JSON output.

near_misses.failure_mode: Independent plugin/MCP mutation steps could produce order-dependent provider argv or make inspection describe a different launch than the process actually executes.
near_misses.durable_control: One ResolvedLaunch performs deterministic plugin-then-MCP activation composition and is consumed by both inspection and the real process launch; ordering and clean/plugin-only/MCP-only compatibility are regression-tested.

artifact_capability_gates.requirement: Exercise exact v0.5.0 PR-candidate bytes on macOS Apple Silicon with pinned Codex 0.160.0; require one qualified whole plugin plus one qualified root-user stdio MCP in the same launch, usable runtime evidence for both, admitted-env canary only, sibling absence, fail-closed overlap/drift/config-layer negatives and task-owned lifecycle closure.

Build the exact future shipping v0.5.0 archive once from accepted main and requalify clean, whole-plugin, standalone-MCP and composed plugin+MCP Codex capabilities against frozen exact provider inputs before tag creation.
Preserve exact v0.5.0 candidate qualification of the unchanged Claude clean and bounded skill-only whole-plugin paths on pinned Claude Code 2.1.289 without widening Claude standalone MCP authority.
Materialize exact v0.5.0 release facts, notes and publish preview, require semantic public-claim PASS, and bind the accepted digests into pretag evidence before tag.
After separate Owner publish approval, use only the canonical guarded publish helper with exact Draft/tag/payload revalidation and authoritative reconciliation.
Verify the actual Latest Release, releases/latest/download bytes, attestations and isolated public installer route before reporting PUBLIC_INSTALL_VERIFIED.

product_outcome: Ship v0.5.0 as the minimal shared Codex launch-composition foundation: one typed resolved launch can preserve clean/plugin-only/MCP-only behavior, safely compose exactly one qualified whole plugin with exactly one qualified standalone stdio MCP, expose sanitized human/JSON inspection from the same truth, and remain fail-closed under conflict, environment, sibling and source-drift conditions.

contract_evolution_review.rationale: v0.5.0 adds a new blocker-producing provider capability: two previously separate bounded Codex resource paths can now coexist in one launch. The release contract therefore expands only enough to require exact-candidate mixed runtime rehearsal, accepted-main preservation of that evidence and privacy/atomicity regressions for the shared ResolvedLaunch.
promoted_controls: single typed ResolvedLaunch shared by human/JSON inspection and real Codex launch
bounded zero/one whole-plugin plus zero/one standalone-stdio-MCP composition with deterministic activation ordering
fail-closed plugin/MCP identity-overlap and raw provider activation-conflict checks
both selected source plans revalidated at action time; one-side drift invalidates the whole composed launch

exact-PR macOS real-provider composition rehearsal bound to exact candidate/provider bytes
